summary: All fifteen findings confirmed; several fixes are replaced. /1: the §4.2 lemmas are misordered, but moving them to AI.5 as proposed would create a cycle (AI.2's Lemma 4.26 uses Proposition 4.13, and RS-01 moves only the lemmas already tagged AI.5 in the CP decomposition); move items 051–056 to AI.0, keep 062–068 at AI.2, and send RS-01's Lemma 4.9 to the maintainer. /2: owner CR.3:Frobenius-isogeny with a link to AI.5. /3: item 085 (Scholze finiteness) has the same cycle and must move with Theorem 5.7; P8:local-rational needs widening. /4: AI.0 is not upstream of CR.4, so move the Witt-vector results to AI.0 and add a link AI.0 → CR.4. /5: CP.5, plus Lang's lifting of singular Enriques surfaces. /6: the almost-purity comparisons are planned (AI.3, and PAPER-SCHOLZE-13's routes); W_r(𝔪) is idempotent (Cor. 10.2), only W(𝔪^♭) is not. /7: the Lemma 3.20 counterexample holds (error, a stated result; require continuity of Q_p → R rather than 'any Tate Q_p-algebra'). /8–/10 confirmed with small corrections (Lemma 12.8(iv) has four occurrences; two entries become errors affecting the proof). /12: Beauville–Laszlo, Gabber–Ramero, Kiehl and Scholze 2012 Lemma 5.6 are already planned. /15: eight more off-by-one locators. /11, /13, /14 confirmed.

findings.reason: Two of the finding's three claims are right: the ordering error and the triple planning. Its main claim is wrong: RS-01 does not move this package to AI.5. Its main fix would create a cycle and must not be applied. (a) Ordering, checked. Lemma 4.9 (item 065, route 3, AI.2) is proved using the coherence of W_n(O♭) and Lemmas 3.25–3.26. Published p. 269: 'We freely use Lemma 3.25 and Lemma 3.26', and 'since W_n(O♭) is coherent, pM ⊂ M is finitely presented'. Proposition 4.13 (item 068, planned at AI.2) takes its part (i) from Lemma 4.9. The coherence items 051–056 go to AI.3 (route 4). I computed reachability over the atlas stage edges plus the links of every accepted restructuring and link map: AI.3 is not upstream of AI.2, whose requirements are AI.0, P7:annulus-foundations, R06.1 and RF4:vector-bundles. (b) Triple planning, checked. The accepted CohomologyComparisons decomposition and the draft packet state the same results as CP.0/coherence-of-witt-vectors-of-perfectoid-integers, CP.5/perfectness-and-tor-bounds-for-ainf-modules and CP.5/ainf-module-structure-theorem. The CP.0 coverage note reads 'the coherence node is naturally AInfCohomology:AI.0 (or AI.2) material'. (c) The claim about RS-01 is wrong. RS-01's owner entry covers the §4.2 lemmas 'already tagged AI.5 supplier material in the partial CP decomposition'; the finding's quotation drops exactly this qualifier. In that accepted decomposition only Lemma 4.9 is tagged AI.5 among these items; the other AI.5 tags are Lemmas 4.14, 4.16, 4.19 and Corollaries 4.15, 4.17, 4.20. The structure-theorem node, whose proof contains Kedlaya's Lemma 4.6, Lemmas 4.7, 4.8, 4.10 and Corollary 4.12, is tagged 'owned by AInfCohomology:AI.2 per its stage description (torsion decompositions)'. The decomposition's ownership gap says 'AI.2 owns BKF modules, torsion decompositions (Proposition 4.13) and Fargues' equivalence'. RS-01 lists no change to AI.2, so under §15 AI.2 keeps its text, which plans 'torsion decompositions and the étale/Witt specializations'. RS-01's own ledger keeps 'finitely presented BKF data and valid operations' at AI.2. (d) The proposed move creates a cycle. Lemma 4.26 (item 079) is planned at AI.2 and is one of AI.2's named sources. It is stated for every BKF module, and its proof reduces 'to the case where M is finite free, using Proposition 4.13' (published p. 278). AI.5 requires AI.2, so Proposition 4.13 and its inputs (items 062–064, 066, 067) cannot move to AI.5. The one real conflict with RS-01 is Lemma 4.9 (item 065). RS-01 assigns it to AI.5, but Proposition 4.13 at AI.2 needs it, so that assignment cannot be carried out without a cycle. Right fix: (1) Move items 051–056 to AInfCohomology:AI.0, which is upstream of AI.2, AI.3, AI.5 and CP.0, and update routes 1 and 4. (2) Keep items 062–064, 066 and 067 in route 3, and keep item 068 planned at AI.2. Rewrite route 3's reason to cite the AI.2 tag in the accepted CP decomposition and Lemma 4.26's use of Proposition 4.13. (3) Keep item 065 at AI.2, or move it to AI.0 together with coherence. Add a maintainer note that RS-01's assignment of the CP.5 perfectness-and-Tor node to AI.5 conflicts with AI.2's Proposition 4.13, and that the owner must be AI.2 or AI.0. (4) Record the aliases: CP.0/coherence-of-witt-vectors-of-perfectoid-integers becomes an alias of the AI.0 node. CP.5/perfectness-and-tor-bounds-for-ainf-modules and CP.5/ainf-module-structure-theorem become aliases of the AI.2 nodes, not the AI.5 nodes the finding names.

The cycle is real. The proof of Theorem 14.3 (published p. 392) says: 'It follows that all cohomology groups are finite free after inverting p by Corollary 4.20 and comparisons (iii) and (iv), using also Proposition 13.21. Thus, all cohomology groups are Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules.' Item 009 is planned at AI.5 and item 189 (Proposition 13.21) at CP.2. CP.2 requires AI.5 directly. Proposition 13.21 (pp. 387–388) is purely crystalline. Its proof has two steps: Frobenius on H^i_crys(Z/A_crys) is an isomorphism after inverting p for qcqs smooth O/p-schemes, and crystalline base change along Y ×_{O/p} O/p^{1/p^n} ≅ Ȳ ×_k O/p^{1/p^n}. The accepted CohomologyComparisons decomposition already records this cycle and recommends moving Proposition 13.21 upstream, 'CrystallineCohomology CR.3 as a Berthelot–Ogus-type base change, or AI.4'. The fix needs two refinements. (1) The rational Frobenius-isogeny is not in the early CR.3 stage. CR.3's text says 'Its rational-isogeny conclusion is a later substage, proved through CR.4's de Rham–Witt/Cartier control'. That substage is CrystallineCohomology:CR.3:Frobenius-isogeny, which requires CR.3 and CR.4. The owner should therefore be CR.3:Frobenius-isogeny, with the link CR.3:Frobenius-isogeny → AInfCohomology:AI.5. I checked that this is acyclic: AI.5 is upstream of none of CR.3, CR.4 or the substage. (2) No CR.3 text states Proposition 13.21 itself; CP.2's text is what currently claims it. So item 189 should become missing and be routed to CR.3:Frobenius-isogeny by a source route; CR.3 names BMS1 §14 as a source. Add a maintainer note that CP.2's line 'Prove the relevant crystalline change-of-base/invariance statement after p-inversion' becomes an import. That note should also say the substage must cover smooth affine, non-proper schemes, which the proof's first step needs; the CP decomposition flags this scope question. CP.2 then receives the result through AI.5. Add a request from AI.5 to CR.3:Frobenius-isogeny, and state the dependency in route 6's reason. Item 009's note already records it. The finding's alternative, giving Proposition 13.21 to AI.5, needs the same link, because AI.5 has no CR.3 ancestor. Without that link the alternative is still misordered.

The evidence checks out. Theorem 5.7 (published p. 286) is headed '[Scholze, proof of Theorem 8.4]'. It is used for part (iv) of Theorem 14.3 (p. 392), and p. 287 derives from it RΓ_et(X_C, Z_p) ⊗ B_dR^+ ≅ RΓ_proet(X_C, B_dR,X^+). The proof of Theorem 13.1 (p. 385) uses exactly that isomorphism. PAPER-SCHOLZE-13's review accepts route 1. That route sends s5-thm5.1-primitive-comparison and s1-thm1.3-primitive-comparison-absolute to the pair [P8, P8:local-rational] without choosing one. Reachability, checked over the atlas stage edges plus accepted restructuring and link-map links: - AI.4 is upstream of P8, through AI.5 → CP.2 or AI.6 → CP.4 → P8. - P8:local-rational is not upstream of AI.4, and AI.4 is not upstream of CP.3. - The link P8:local-rational → CP.3 already exists. - Adding P8:local-rational → AI.4, or AI.4 → CP.3, is acyclic. So the étale specialization of Theorem 14.3 and the B_dR^+ step of Theorem 13.1 have no upstream supplier. Three additions to the fix: (a) Item 085, Scholze's finiteness of H^i_et(X_C, Z_p) (route 14, sent to P8), has the same cycle. The BMS1 proof of Theorem 14.3 applies Corollary 4.20, whose hypothesis that H^j(C)[1/pμ] be free over A_inf[1/pμ] needs H^j_et(X, Z_p) to be finitely generated; the accepted CP decomposition records this implicit use. Finiteness and the primitive comparison are the two halves of Scholze's Theorem 5.1, so route 14 must move to the same upstream stage as the primitive comparison. (b) P8:local-rational fits by order. Its requirements are AI.3, A1, H0, R06.1 and P3, plus the RS-05 links from D0, E1, R0, R3, P2 and P7, and none of these lies downstream of AI.4. But its text says 'construct only the rational relative period sheaves, local acyclicity, strictness and local Poincaré lemma'. A global primitive comparison and finiteness theorem therefore needs a maintainer note to widen that stage, or an early substage with the same requirements. (c) For item 018, prefer stating the B_dR^+ consequence at the same stage as the primitive comparison over adding AI.4 → CP.3. PAPER-SCHOLZE-13's own B_dR^+ comparison (s8-thm8.4a) is planned at P8, which is downstream of CP.3, so it does not help CP.3. Item 092 itself may stay at AI.4, because its only real consumer, Theorem 14.3(iv), is at AI.5, downstream. The finding's disclosure is noted and does not affect the verdict.

Published p. 324: 'W_r(O)⟨U^{±1/p^∞}⟩ = W_r(O⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩) by passing to the p-adic completion in Lemma 9.8 below'. - Theorem 10.4 (item 149) is used in Remark 9.10 and in the proof of Lemma 9.9 (item 139, AI.3). Published p. 326: 'By Theorem 10.4, …'. - CR.4 requires AI.1 and CR.2 and is not upstream of AI.3. - Corollary 10.2 (item 147) is weaker evidence. It is cited only in the remark after the statement of Corollary 3.29 (p. 261), not in its proof. It is used implicitly wherever §9 works in the almost setting W_r(𝔪) ⊂ W_r(O), for example Lemma 9.7(iii), so including it is reasonable. The primary fix, as justified, is wrong. It says 'AI.0 is upstream … through AI.1, of CR.4'. That is false: AI.1 requires only DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1 and EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1, and there is no path from AI.0 to CR.4. In the relevant roadmaps CR.4's ancestors are AI.1, CR.0–CR.2 and E1. CR.4's own content also uses these results: - Lemma 10.8 (item 152, planned at CR.4) removes Langer–Zink's hypothesis with Theorem 10.4. - Proposition 10.14 (item 157, route 11) uses Theorem 10.4 in the second step of its proof. - Lemma 10.9(ii) (item 153) uses Lemma 10.1. Moving items 138, 146, 147 and 149 to AI.0 alone would therefore just move the ordering error to CR.4. Right fix: move items 138, 146, 147 and 149 to AInfCohomology:AI.0 as proposed, and add the stage link AI.0 → CrystallineCohomology:CR.4 in the same change. That link is acyclic because CR.4 is not upstream of AI.0. Update routes 1, 4 and 11. The finding's alternative, the link CR.4 → AI.3, is also acyclic and valid, but it makes the local AΩ construction wait for crystalline cohomology (CR.2), which cuts against AI.3's design. It is second choice. Either way, the notes of items 137, 139 and 056 should name where they import Lemma 9.8, Theorem 10.4 and Corollary 10.2 from.

Checked in the published text. The paper uses four comparisons. (1) p. 306: 'By Faltings' almost purity theorem, the map RΓ_cont(Γ, R_∞) → RΓ_cont(Δ, R̄^) is an almost quasi-isomorphism'. (2) p. 307: its identification with RΓ(X_profét, Ô^+_X) via Scholze 2013, Propositions 3.5 and 3.7(iii) and Corollary 6.6, and the almost quasi-isomorphisms between the Ω̃ variants via Scholze 2013, Lemma 4.10(v). (3) Display (2) on p. 230 for A_inf(R_∞), almost 'with respect to the ideal [𝔪^♭]', and the W_r version in the proof of Corollary 9.11 (p. 327), which applies Lemma 8.11 with I = W_r(𝔪). (4) Condition (i) of Lemma 9.12, 'immediate from the almost purity theorem' in Proposition 9.14 (p. 330) and in Lemma 12.8 (p. 366). None of the 190 items states any of these as a theorem. Item 121 is a definition that mentions the Ô^+ case in passing, and item 134's note refers to it. The theorem the abstract names as the construction's foundation should be an item. It is planned rather than missing, as the finding says. AI.3 says 'prove the almost purity comparison' and requires PerfectoidSpaces:P3, whose accepted decomposition has an almost-purity-theorem node. The identification (2) is planned through the accepted PAPER-SCHOLZE-13: Proposition 3.5 at AdicEtaleGeometry:A1, Proposition 3.7(iii) at ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0, and Lemma 4.10(v) and Corollary 6.6 routed to AI.3 (its route 5). Medium severity is fair. One claim is wrong: the finding says the W_r(𝔪) and W(𝔪^♭) variants both fail idempotence. Only W(𝔪^♭) ⊂ A_inf fails, as p. 327 warns. Corollary 10.2 (p. 334, item 147) proves W_r(𝔪)^2 = W_r(𝔪), with W_r(𝔪) an increasing union of principal ideals generated by non-zero-divisors. [𝔪^♭] is idempotent too, since [x] = [x^{1/p}][x^{1−1/p}]. The paper uses 'almost' only for idempotent ideals: 𝔪, 𝔪^♭, W_r(𝔪) and [𝔪^♭]. Lemma 9.12(i) passes to D(O^♭) precisely to avoid W(𝔪^♭), which appears only as an annihilator (Theorem 5.7 and the remark after Lemma 5.6). RS-05 gives PerfectoidSpaces:P0 almost algebra over an admissible idempotent ideal, and its accepted decomposition has a node for (K°, 𝔪). So a W(𝔪^♭) almost notion cannot be planned at P0. Right fix: (a) as proposed, splitting item 121 into its definition and a theorem item. Plan the comparison at AI.3 with the almost purity theorem from P3, and cite the identification's owners: A1 for Proposition 3.5, H0 for Proposition 3.7(iii), and AI.3 for Lemma 4.10(v) and Corollary 6.6. (b) as proposed, at AI.3: the W_r version relative to W_r(𝔪), the A_inf version relative to [𝔪^♭], and the mod-p version in D(O^♭) relative to 𝔪^♭ of Lemma 9.12(i). (c) Almost zero modules and almost quasi-isomorphisms relative to an idempotent ideal, planned at P0 and instantiated for 𝔪, 𝔪^♭, [𝔪^♭] and W_r(𝔪); the last uses Corollary 10.2 (item 147). Do not plan a W(𝔪^♭) almost notion at P0. Instead note on items 091, 092 and 140 that W(𝔪^♭) is not idempotent, so 'killed by W(𝔪^♭)' is a plain annihilation statement.

Confirmed. Checked at TeX (Lemma lemma_Tate_perfectoid and its proof) and the published pp. 255-256; the text is identical in both, and item 047 copies the converse. The counterexample holds; I checked every step. A = (p,T)-adic completion of O_C[T^{1/p^inf}] consists of sums of c_e T^e (e >= 0 in Z[1/p]) with, for each n, only finitely many e < n having v_p(c_e) < n. (1) A is T-adically and p-adically complete (a ring complete for the finitely generated ideal (p,T) is complete for any smaller finitely generated ideal), T is a non-zero-divisor, so R = A[1/T] with the T-adic topology on A is a complete Tate ring with ring of definition A; A is open and bounded, so its elements are power-bounded. (2) For r > 0 the Gauss valuation v_r(sum c_e T^e) = min_e(v_p(c_e) + r e) is attained (finitely many candidates below any bound) and multiplicative (use the smallest exponent achieving the minimum in each factor), and extends to R. If x = g/T^k is integral over A, the usual ultrametric argument gives v_r(x) >= 0, i.e. v_r(g) >= rk for every r > 0; letting r go to infinity forces c_e = 0 for e < k, and g/T^k is then in A. So A is integrally closed in R, hence a ring of integral elements. The same argument applied to a power-bounded x (v_r(x^n) >= -rm for all n) shows R° = A. (3) A/p is the T-adically completed (O_C/p)[T^{1/p^inf}], similarly A/p^{1/p}, and Frobenius A/p^{1/p} -> A/p is c_e T^e -> c_e^p T^{pe}, a bijection because O_C/p^{1/p} -> O_C/p is. As p^{1/p} is a non-zero-divisor with (p^{1/p})^p = p and A is p^{1/p}-adically complete, A is perfectoid by Lemma 3.10(ii). (4) R is not perfectoid in Fontaine's sense. The shortest argument: if pi is a topologically nilpotent unit with p = pi^p w, w in R°, then p^n = pi^{pn} w^n tends to 0, so Fontaine-perfectoid rings have p topologically nilpotent; but the continuous ring map A -> O_C, sum c_e T^e -> c_0, kills TA and sends p^n to p^n, so no power of p lies in TA and p is not topologically nilpotent in R. (The finding's version, taking the image of pi in O_C, is also right but silently uses pi, w in A, i.e. R° = A, shown in (2).) The proof's last sentence indeed fails: with pi_0 = T one gets pi = T^{1/p^n}, and p/T^{1/p^{n-1}} has negative v_r for large r. With the added hypothesis 'p topologically nilpotent in R' the paper's proof goes through: pick M with p^M in pi_0 R^+; then (p/pi^p)^{p^{n-1}} = p^{p^{n-1}}/(u pi_0) lies in R^+ once p^{n-1} >= M, so p/pi^p is in R^+ because R^+ is integrally closed. The paper only uses the forward direction later (Section 5.1, p. 285: an affinoid perfectoid gives a perfectoid ring R^+). E1-E18 do not contain it. Record as: kind error, affects a stated result, known new (a brief web search found no correction). Two adjustments to the fix. First, the parenthetical 'for example any Tate Q_p-algebra' is too loose: an abstract Q_p-algebra structure does not make p topologically nilpotent (Q_p((T)) with ring of definition Q_p[[T]] is a counterexample); say 'for example any Tate ring whose structure map from Q_p (or K) is continuous, such as a Banach Q_p-algebra'. Second, the paragraph after the lemma needs no correction: it only concerns rings that are already Fontaine-perfectoid (in which p is automatically topologically nilpotent) and Scholze's and Kedlaya-Liu's perfectoid algebras, which are topological K- and Q_p-algebras. It does not use the converse. Item 047's last sentence may stay, reading 'K-algebra' as a topological K-algebra. Only the converse needs the hypothesis. The stages PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra and PerfectoidSpaces:P1 do not state the converse in their atlas descriptions, so the check the fix asks for concerns only their future decompositions.

Confirmed. Checked in the TeX (lemma_existence_of_structure_maps_for_torus and lemma_explicit_decomposition_of_Wtor) and on the published pp. 351-352 (page image); the slips are identical in both, and none of them is among E1-E18 (E11-E14 concern other passages of Section 11). (1) In the proof, H^0(D/xi~_r) = W_r(O)[U^{±1/p^inf}]^{Z^d} with gamma_i sending U_i^{1/p^s} to [zeta_{p^{r+s}}]U_i^{1/p^s}. So gamma_i(U_i) = [zeta_{p^r}]U_i. Since [zeta_{p^r}] - 1 is a non-zero-divisor of W_r(O) (Proposition 3.17(i)), no non-zero multiple of U_i is invariant, so U_i is not in W_r^0(D) and lambda_r([T_i]) = U_i cannot hold. The proof's own identification U_i^{1/p^s} -> [T_i^{1/p^{r+s}}] sends U_i^{p^r} to [T_i]. Compatibility with R, which in degree 0 is phi_D^{-1} (Section 11.1: R' is induced by phi_D^{-1}, and R = R' in degree 0), gives the same answer: phi_D^{-1}(U_i^{p^{r+1}}) = U_i^{p^r}, whereas the printed U_i would need phi_D^{-1}(U_i) = U_i. F is the canonical projection, which is compatible with [T_i] -> [T_i]^p. So the right normalization is lambda_r([T_i]) = U_i^{p^r}. The rest of Section 11.2 (Corollary 11.12, Theorem 11.13) only uses the lambda_r built in the proof, so nothing downstream changes. (2) The sentence before the lemma prints lambda_r: W_r(O)[T^{±1}] -> W_r^0(D). It should read W_r(O[T^{±1}]), as in the lemma and as an F-V-procomplex requires. (3) Proof of Lemma 11.9, p. 351: with u = u(p^{-r}a) = max(r - min_i v_p(a(i)), 0) (Section 10.4), each ([zeta_{p^r}^{a(i)}]-1)/([zeta_{p^r}]-1) is divisible by ([zeta_{p^u}]-1)/([zeta_{p^r}]-1), and one of them equals it up to a unit. The printed ([zeta_{p^r}^{u}]-1)/([zeta_{p^r}]-1) is the integer power. For r = 2, d = 1, a(1) = p we get u = 1 and the printed element is 1. Its Koszul complex is acyclic, whereas the correct element ([zeta_p]-1)/([zeta_{p^2}]-1) gives W_1(O) = O in degrees 0 and 1 by Corollary 3.18(iii), as the lemma asserts. The element is printed three times (the divisor, the Ann and the quotient); all three need the correction. Record all three as kind misprint, affects nothing, known new: the intended meaning is fixed by the surrounding proof. Item 162 must be corrected to lambda_r([T_i]) = U_i^{p^r}. Minor: the finding's evidence says the quoted proof lines are on 'the same page' (p. 351), but the H^0 formula and the identification are on p. 352.

Confirmed, all three, with one classification refinement. None is among E1-E18, and each is in the published text at the page given. (a) Lemma 6.9, published pp. 291-292 (TeX lem:mapLetabackforth). Take (eta_I C)^i = {x in C^i : dx in I C^{i+1}} tensored with I^{⊗i} (Definition in Section 6.1). For I = (p) over Z and C = Z in degree n-1 (p-torsion-free, H^n(C)[p] = 0), (eta_p C)^{n-1} = p^{n-1}Z, which is not contained in p^n Z = I^{⊗n} C^{n-1}. The paper's 'quotient' is then not even defined: the image of p^{n-1}Z in Q/p^nZ is Z/p, not H^n(C)[p] = 0. The correct statement, for I-torsion-free C, is the following. The map x = f^{n-1}w -> class of dw/f is an isomorphism (eta_I C)^{n-1}/(I^{⊗n}C^{n-1} + I^{⊗(n-1)}Z^{n-1}) ≅ I^{⊗(n-1)} ⊗ H^n(C)[I]. So under the hypothesis, (eta_I C)^{n-1} = I^{⊗n}C^{n-1} + I^{⊗(n-1)}Z^{n-1}. That gives d((eta_I C)^{n-1}) ⊂ I^{⊗n}B^n, which is exactly what is needed for the map to I^{⊗n} ⊗ tau^{>=n}C (with (tau^{>=n}C)^n = C^n/B^n). Kind error, affects the proof. (b) Lemma 4.8, p. 268. K is any perfectoid field (Section 4.2). For K = C the value group of C^flat is p^Q, and D = {x : |x| <= p^{-sqrt 2}} is a rank-one submodule that is neither principal, nor m^flat·J with J principal, nor K^flat. The lemma survives: a non-principal D has no element of maximal absolute value, so every x in D is (x/y)·y with |x/y| < 1 and y in D; hence m^flat D = D and D ⊗ k = 0. E2's reason ('the three cases classify rank-one submodules') repeats the false claim, and the suggested rewording is correct. Kind error (or gap), affects the proof. (c) Theorem 14.5(ii), published p. 393. For Q = W(k)[1/p]/W(k), Q/p^n = 0 but Tor_1(Q, W(k)/p^n) = Q[p^n] ≅ W(k)/p^n has length n. For finitely generated torsion Q, a sum of W(k)/p^{a_j}, both sides have length sum_j min(a_j, n). In the proof Q = N/M is finitely generated, so the inequality is proved.
